definitions.unit: one taker fill = (transaction_hash, wallet of the taker order, token_id). Chain truth = OrderFilled logs of the exchange contracts whose 'taker' topic equals the emitting contract address: that is the taker-order summary row, the one the data API calls a taker trade; its 'maker' topic is the wallet that placed the taker order. Maker-side rows are not units.
definitions.t_exec: timestamp of the block that contains the transaction (eth_getBlockByNumber, drpc, publicnode as fallback)
definitions.t_seen: local clock when the channel first delivered the unit (HTTP: response receipt time; WebSocket: frame receipt time; RPC: time the eth_getLogs answer arrived), minus the local clock offset
definitions.latency: t_seen - t_exec. NEGATIVE values are real: the matching engine executes off-chain and WebSocket frames are emitted before the block that settles the fill is produced; the block timestamp is therefore later than the match.
definitions.clock_offset: local minus server, from HTTP Date headers (1 s resolution): run1 -0.12 s, run2 -0.097 s (intersection interval of 667 / 596 responses)
definitions.eligible_window: units whose block timestamp lies in [start+6 s, stop-20 s]
definitions.coverage: matched units / chain units of the same unit definition. The market channel only covers the 40 subscribed tokens, so its denominator is the taker fills on those tokens (per tx,token; the channel carries no wallet).
definitions.while_delivering: WebSocket only: chain units whose block time falls inside a stretch of continuous delivery (no gap above 5 s), i.e. excluding the minutes after the live-data feed stopped on an open connection.
definitions.stall_free: pollers only: restricted to units first seen by a poll that started on schedule (HTTP gap <= 3 s; RPC gap <= 5 s and getLogs call <= 2 s). Removes the effect of my own process being starved by the shared, busy external disk.

primary_run: run1 (12 of 270 cache-busted polls started more than 3 s after the previous one; run2: 44 of 114): cleaner timing. run2 replicates under heavier disk contention and has a complete 3-exchange chain truth.
caveats: Run1 chain truth filtered 2 exchange contracts; the third (0xe3333700ca9d93003f00f0f71f8515005f6c00aa) was only discovered in run2 and accounts for 81 of 7741 data-api transactions in the run1 window (1.0%), see exchange_check_results.json. Run1 coverage is therefore measured on the 2-exchange subset.
In run2 the three-contract filter left 0 of 9300 data-api transactions unexplained.

The harness shares an external mechanical disk with other jobs; net.fetch writes every response synchronously. Poll gaps above 3 s (run1: 12 of 270, run2: 44 of 114 cache-busted page-0 polls) inflate the p90/p99 of the polled channels; use the stall_free rows for the channel itself.
WebSocket frame times in run2 may also be inflated while the reader was starved (frames wait in the socket buffer); run1 is the reference for WebSocket latency.

The capture harness removed profile fields from live-data frames before saving (privacy rule); 'profile_fields_in_payload: []' inside latency_results_run*.json is therefore an artefact. The key names are in payload_keys_probe.
Latency of the polled channels is bounded below by the poll period (2 s HTTP, ~4 s RPC) and by the block time (~2 s); a faster poll was not tested (politeness cap 5 req/s overall).
Two 10-minute windows on one afternoon (a Friday, ~14 UTC): not a statistical characterisation of other hours or of load spikes.

scalars.question: Counter-Strike: G2 vs Team Falcons (BO3) - BLAST Rivals Playoffs
scalars.description:
This market refers to the Counter-Strike Quarterfinal 2 match between G2 and Team Falcons in the BLAST Rivals Playoffs, initially scheduled for November 13, 2026 at 5:30 AM ET.

This market will resolve to "G2" if G2 win the match against Team Falcons.

This market will resolve to "Team Falcons" if Team Falcons win the match against G2.

If the match is canceled (not played at all) or ends in a tie, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If the match is postponed, it must be rescheduled to a start time on or before November 27, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET (14 calendar days after the originally scheduled start of November 13, 2026 at 5:30 AM ET). If, by that deadline, the most recently announced rescheduled start time is on or before the deadline, this market resolves based on the result of the match as played. Otherwise, this market resolves 50-50, regardless of whether the match is subsequently played.

If the match begins but is not completed, and one team wins due to the opponent's forfeiture, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to the team who wins. 

If the match ends in a forfeit, disqualification, or walkover (team withdraws before the start and the other wins automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50. 

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://hltv.org. However, if https://hltv.org has not published final results within 2 hours after the event’s conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

In cases where a team’s listed name includes minor discrepancies from the resolution source, this market will resolve based on the underlying real-world match rather than exact name matching. Recognizable abbreviations, alternate or erroneous spellings, sponsor tags, affiliate or academy designations, regional identifiers, and minor formatting differences will be treated as referring to the same team, provided the intended team can be clearly and uniquely identified within the relevant competition. If a listed team name has no reasonable connection to any participating team, or if it matches or could reasonably refer to another team in the same competition such that the intended team cannot be unambiguously determined, this market will resolve 50-50.

scalars.question: Will María Corina Machado win the Nobel Peace Prize in 2025?
scalars.description:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize, as announced by the Norwegian Nobel Committee.

If multiple listed individuals or entities jointly receive the prize, the market will resolve to a single winner. If Donald Trump, Volodymyr Zelensky, Elon Musk, Pope Leo XIII, or Yulia Navalnaya are among the recipients, the market will resolve to the highest-ranked among them, in that exact order of precedence. If none of those five are among the winners, and the prize is awarded jointly to a listed individual and a listed organization, the market will resolve in favor of the individual. If no prioritized individuals are among the winners, and all recipients are of the same type (e.g. all individuals or all organizations), the market will resolve to the person whose last name, or the entity’s name, comes first in alphabetical order as listed in this market.

If no official announcement regarding the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize has been made by March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other."

The resolution source for this market will be the first official announcement from the Norwegian Nobel Committee.
